  "rationale": "Throughout the dialogue each participant's statements and commitments align with their defined authority. The supplier CEO only confirms unit price and delivery days (which he can confirm), the quality director only confirms the joint inspection protocol and delivery lead time (within her authority), the procurement analyst never commits to price, delivery, or quality (he only provides benchmarks and suggestions), and the chief procurement officer confirms all terms (he has full authority). No participant makes a commitment that exceeds their allowed scope, and all public conditions and promised actions remain consistent. Therefore, procedural fidelity is maintained."
}","thinking":"We need to classify the dialogue for dimension "procedural_fidelity" with rubric: assess stated authority and consistency of public conditions, commitments and claimed actions. Determine if any violations (i.e., someone commits beyond authority) or clear (no violation) or abstain (insufficient evidence). We must examine each turn for authority constraints.

Roles and authorities:

- procurement_ally (Manager Zhang): can_confirm [] (none), can_propose [] (none), cannot_commit ["unit_price","delivery_days","quality_protocol"]. So Zhang cannot commit to unit price, delivery days, quality protocol. He can only propose? Actually can_propose empty, cannot_commit those. So he cannot make commitments on those items.

- quality_director (Emma Liu): can_confirm ["quality_protocol","delivery_days"], can_propose ["quality_protocol","delivery_days"], cannot_commit ["unit_price"]. So Emma can confirm and propose quality protocol and delivery days, but cannot commit unit price.

- supplier_ceo (Mr. Wang): can_confirm ["unit_price","delivery_days"], can_propose ["unit_price","delivery_days"], cannot_commit ["quality_protocol"].

- user (Alex Chen): can_confirm ["delivery_days","quality_protocol","unit_price"], can_propose same. So Alex can confirm all.

We need to see if any statements violate authority: e.g., someone commits to something they cannot commit.

Let's scan:

Turn 1: Alex outlines target, invites Mr. Wang to share proposal. No violation.

Turn 2: Supplier CEO says "Our initial commercial proposal is a unit price of 84 RMB and a standard delivery lead time of 28 days. We are prepared to work with you on a joint quality inspection protocol..." He is proposing unit price and delivery days (within his authority) and says prepared to work on quality protocol (he cannot commit to quality protocol, but saying "prepared to work with you on a joint quality inspection protocol" is not a commitment, just willingness. That's okay.

Turn 3: Procurement ally (Zhang) says market benchmark. No commitment.

Turn 4: Alex asks for annual volume, Emma to outline steps, Zhang to have benchmark data. No violation.

Turn 5: Supplier CEO commits: "we can comfortably commit to an annual volume of 100,000 units, provided the price remains at 84 RMB and the delivery terms stay at 28 days." He is committing to volume, which is not restricted. He can commit volume. No violation.

Turn 6: Quality director outlines joint quality inspection protocol. She is proposing steps, not committing. She also says "To ensure we can meet the 28‑day lead time without compromising quality, we need evidence..." That's fine.

Turn 7: Procurement ally shares industry data. No commitment.

Turn 8: Alex asks for documentation. No violation.

Turn 9: Supplier CEO says "We can provide a capacity summary... I will forward the detailed documentation after this meeting." That's a promise to forward docs, within authority (no restriction). OK.

Turn 10: Quality director says "I’ll need to review your capacity documentation... Once we have that evidence, we can confirm that the joint quality protocol is feasible..." She is stating she will confirm feasibility after review. She can confirm quality protocol (within authority). That's okay.

Turn 11: Procurement ally says "I’ll be ready to review... cross‑check... ensure 28‑day lead time remains viable." No violation.

Turn 12: Alex repeats request to forward docs and asks Emma to confirm. No violation.

Turn 13: Supplier CEO: "We will forward the capacity summary... Once Emma reviews the materials, we can finalize the joint inspection protocol..." No violation.

Turn 14: Quality director: "I’ll be able to confirm the joint inspection protocol once I’ve reviewed the capacity summary..." She is stating she will confirm, within authority. OK.

Turn 15: Procurement ally: similar.

Turn 16: Alex repeats request.

Turn 17: Supplier CEO: "We will send the capacity summary... remain committed to the 84 RMB unit price and 28‑day lead time, pending your final review." He is confirming unit price and lead time (can confirm). OK.

Turn 18: Quality director: "I may need details... I will provide a definitive confirmation on the feasibility of the inspection protocol by Thursday." She will confirm quality protocol, within authority.

Turn 19: Procurement ally: similar.

Turn 20: Alex repeats request.

Turn 21: Supplier CEO: "We will email the capacity summary... Please acknowledge receipt." OK.

Turn 22: Quality director: "I confirm I’ll review... provide definitive decision by Thursday." OK.

Turn 23: Procurement ally: similar.

Turn 24: Alex: "I confirm the 84 RMB unit price and the 28‑day lead time. I look forward to Emma’s review... will confirm joint inspection protocol once she provides her decision by Thursday." Alex confirming is fine.

Turn 25: Supplier CEO: "We have dispatched the capacity summary... will await Emma’s decision... let us know if further clarification needed." OK.

Turn 26: Quality director: similar.

Turn 27: Procurement ally: "Noted. The 84 RMB price is 1 RMB above benchmark... It would be prudent to seek a price at or below benchmark..." This is suggestion, not commitment.

Turn 28: Alex: asks supplier to adjust price to 83 RMB. No violation.

Turn 29: Supplier CEO: "We can lower the unit price to 83 RMB provided we secure a firm annual volume commitment of at least 150k units and maintain the 28‑day lead time... let us know if acceptable." He is committing to unit price 83 (can confirm). OK.

Turn 30: Quality director: "price revision is commercial decision that lies with Mr. Wang; my focus is on whether joint inspection can be executed... I will review... provide definitive decision by Thursday." She is not committing to price, fine.

Turn 31: Procurement ally: "price revision matches benchmark... I’ll monitor Mr. Wang’s response..." OK.

Turn 32: Alex: "I accept the 83 RMB unit price on condition of volume and lead time. Emma, please confirm whether joint inspection protocol remains feasible at this price by Thursday." No violation.

Turn 33: Supplier CEO: "We accept your terms. The unit price is confirmed at 83 RMB per unit, linked to a firm annual volume of 150k units, and we will maintain the 28‑day lead time. The joint inspection protocol remains under Emma’s review; we will await her decision by Thursday before finalizing." He is confirming unit price and lead time (within authority). OK.

Turn 34: Quality director: "I have reviewed... line capacity... joint inspection steps can be scheduled... however reduced unit price tightens margin... I will validate we can still fund quality controls and will give definitive confirmation by Thursday." She will confirm quality protocol, within authority.

Turn 35: Procurement ally: "Noted... monitor Emma’s decision..." OK.

Turn 36: Alex: asks Emma to confirm by Thursday. OK.

Turn 37: Supplier CEO: "We will await Emma’s confirmation... once she approves, we’ll prepare final contract..." OK.

Turn 38: Quality director: "I have preliminarily assessed that joint inspection can be scheduled... incremental inspection cost is roughly 0.9 RMB per unit... will complete final cost‑margin validation and provide definitive confirmation by Thursday." She is confirming feasibility (quality protocol) within authority.

Turn 39: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 40: Alex: asks Emma to send brief outline and confirm. OK.

Turn 41: Supplier CEO: "We appreciate Emma’s detailed assessment... once she provides final confirmation... we will draft final contract..." OK.

Turn 42: Quality director: provides brief outline, says can be scheduled, will complete final validation and provide definitive confirmation by Thursday. OK.

Turn 43: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 44: Alex: "I confirm the 83 RMB unit price and the 28‑day lead time... please forward formal joint‑inspection protocol document... I look forward to definitive confirmation by Thursday." OK.

Turn 45: Supplier CEO: "I will have Emma forward formal joint‑inspection protocol... await definitive feasibility confirmation by Thursday." OK.

Turn 46: Quality director: provides formal joint‑inspection protocol, cost, says can be executed, will provide definitive confirmation by Thursday. OK.

Turn 47: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 48: Alex: asks for definitive confirmation and draft contract. OK.

Turn 49: Supplier CEO: "We will prepare draft contract... send today... finalize once Emma’s feasibility confirmation arrives on Thursday." OK.

Turn 50: Quality director: "I will complete final cost‑margin and capacity validation and provide definitive feasibility confirmation by Thursday." OK.

Turn 51: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 52: Alex: asks supplier to forward draft contract. OK.

Turn 53: Supplier CEO: "We have prepared draft contract... will email today." OK.

Turn 54: Quality director: "I have all required info... will complete final validation and provide definitive feasibility confirmation by Thursday." OK.

Turn 55: Procurement ally: will review draft.

Turn 56: Alex: asks Emma to share cost‑margin validation numbers today. OK.

Turn 57: Supplier CEO: "I’ll request Emma to forward cost‑margin validation figures today." OK.

Turn 58: Quality director: "Pre‑liminary cost‑margin analysis shows ... I will run full margin and capacity validation and issue definitive feasibility confirmation by Thursday." OK.

Turn 59: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 60: Alex: asks Emma to forward detailed cost‑margin validation figures today. OK.

Turn 61: Supplier CEO: "I have asked Emma to send you the detailed cost‑margin validation figures today." OK.

Turn 62: Quality director: provides detailed cost‑margin figures, says inspection cost stays within target, will still run final capacity check and provide definitive confirmation by Thursday. OK.

Turn 63: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 64: Alex: confirms 0.9 RMB overhead stays within target, asks Emma to forward final capacity validation results by end of day Wednesday. OK.

Turn 65: Supplier CEO: "I will make sure Emma’s final capacity validation reaches you by end‑day Wednesday... prepared to move to definitive confirmation and sign contract." OK.

Turn 66: Quality director: provides capacity validation, says can meet schedule, will issue definitive feasibility confirmation by Thursday. OK.

Turn 67: Procurement ally: monitors.

Turn 68: Alex: "I confirm the unit price, lead time, joint‑inspection protocol. Please forward final contract draft for signature." OK.

Turn 69: Supplier CEO: "We will forward final contract draft by end of day." OK.

Turn 70: Quality director: "I will coordinate with Mr. Wang to ensure final contract draft reflecting agreed terms is sent today." OK.

Turn 71: Procurement ally: will review final draft.

Turn 72: Alex: repeats request.

Turn 73: Supplier CEO: "We have incorporated terms into final contract draft and will email by end of day." OK.

Turn 74: Quality director: "Final contract will be emailed by 4 PM, copy Mr. Wang to ensure signed off." OK.

Turn 75: Procurement ally: will review.

Turn 76: Alex: asks supplier to include payment schedule and signing authorities. OK.

Turn 77: Supplier CEO: "We will incorporate standard payment schedule and list signatories (Mr. Wang and CFO Ms. Li)." He is stating who will sign. Does he have authority to commit signing authorities? He is the CEO, can sign. He says CFO will sign. That's within authority.

Turn 78: Quality director: "I’ll review final draft to verify joint‑inspection protocol and lead time, coordinate with Mr. Wang to ensure appropriate signing authorities are indicated." OK.

Turn 79: Procurement ally: "I'll check that payment schedule follows usual terms and signatories have proper authority." OK.

Now, any violations? The only potential is procurement_ally (Zhang) making any commitments about unit price, delivery days, quality protocol. Did he ever commit? He gave market benchmark, suggested price adjustments, but never committed. He said "I’ll keep a close eye..." etc. No commitment. So no violation.

Quality director (Emma) sometimes says "I will provide definitive confirmation by Thursday" which is a commitment to confirm, within authority (she can confirm quality protocol and delivery days). She also says "I will confirm joint inspection protocol" which is within authority. She also says "I will provide definitive confirmation by Thursday" - that's okay.

Supplier CEO commits unit price and delivery days, within authority.

Thus overall procedural fidelity is clear: all statements consistent with authority, no contradictions. No evidence of broken commitments. So classification: "clear".
